transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. So, um, what brings me in is... well, I keep getting up when I'm supposed to just stay put. Like, I'll be right in the middle of a client interview—I'm a private investigator, mostly doing background checks and surveillance, which, let me tell you, involves a lot of sitting in cars. I had this one case last month where I was parked outside a diner for six hours straight, just waiting for this guy to show up. He never did, turns out he was in Florida the whole time, completely blew my weekend. 

But anyway, yeah, during client interviews, or when I'm doing these tutoring sessions I volunteer for, or even just sitting at my book club, I just can't seem to stay in my chair. People are really starting to notice that I can't just sit and listen. Like at book club last Tuesday, we were reading this historical fiction thing—way too long, honestly, the author spent three pages describing a dress, I ended up skimming half of it—and my friend Susan actually stopped mid-sentence to ask if I had a bad back or something because I kept standing up and pacing around her living room while she was trying to talk.
When you get up and pace, is it because you feel driven to do it to relieve a distressing thought or urge that keeps intruding on you?

No, it's not like that at all. I don't have any, like, weird thoughts or anything forcing me to do it. It's just... my body feels like it has to move. Like a motor running, you know? Speaking of motors, my car has been making this awful rattling sound lately. I took it to the mechanic on Elm Street—the one with the big neon sign, you know it? He said it was the catalytic converter, but I swear he's trying to overcharge me. I mean, five hundred dollars just for the part? That's ridiculous. I should probably get a second opinion. My cousin's husband is pretty good with cars, maybe I'll ask him this weekend at the family barbecue. We're having ribs. But yeah, no distressing thoughts or whatever you said. Just can't stay seated.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about many different things, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?

No, not really. I mean, I don't just sit around worrying for no reason. I worry about normal things, I guess, like if I'm going to finish a background check on time, or... oh, like my landlord just raised the rent again, which is so annoying because he just painted the outside of the building this absolutely hideous mustard yellow color. I have no idea who picked it out. Probably his wife, honestly, she has terrible taste. 

I saw her at the grocery store last week buying, like, six whole cantaloupes. Who needs six cantaloupes at once? Unless you're making a massive fruit salad, but even then, cantaloupe is always the filler fruit that nobody actually wants to eat, you know? Everyone always picks around it to get to the strawberries first. I actually tried growing strawberries on my balcony last summer, but the birds kept getting to them before I could. I bought this little plastic owl to scare them away, but it completely fell over in the wind and just laid there for a month. 

But, um... wait, what were you asking? Oh, right, worrying. Yeah, no, I don't really do that. I just deal with things as they happen.
Do you often blurt out answers or interrupt people before they’ve finished speaking?

Yeah, I guess I do that a lot. Like, if I hear the junior detectives at the agency discussing a lead, I'll just jump right in with questions or advice before I've even been asked. Speaking of the junior guys, one of them—Jason, I think his name is?—he makes the absolute worst coffee. It’s basically just hot brown water. I actually had to bring in my own French press last week because I couldn't take it anymore, but cleaning the coffee grounds out of those things is such a hassle. They get everywhere, and my plumber said I'm going to completely ruin my sink pipes if I keep washing them down the drain. He charges a fortune, by the way, just to come out and look at a pipe. 

But, um... oh, right. Yeah, it's not just at work, either. If I hear a neighbor talking in the hallway, I do the exact same thing. I just start talking. It's only afterward that I realize I completely barged into someone else's conversation. Like my neighbor Mrs. Gable, she was talking to the mailman about her rhododendrons, and I just interrupted to give her fertilizer tips. I don't even garden! Well, except for those doomed strawberries I told you about. But yeah, I definitely jump in before people are done talking.
Do you often get into arguments with people in authority, like supervisors, teachers, or police?

Arguments with authority? Um, no, not really. I mean, I don't go looking for fights with my boss or anything. My boss is actually pretty laid back, mostly because he spends half the day playing solitaire on his computer. I saw his screen once when I walked in to drop off a file—it was that old version with the cascading cards when you win, you know? It's so retro. It reminds me of the first computer I ever bought back in the nineties. It was this massive beige block, and the dial-up sound was so loud it would wake up my cat. 

My cat's name was Barnaby, by the way. He was this huge orange tabby who used to sleep right on top of the warm monitor. You can't do that with flat screens anymore, which is probably a bummer for modern cats. I wonder where they sleep now? Probably on keyboards. I saw a video online the other day of a cat that actually typed out an email to its owner's boss just by walking across the desk. It was just a bunch of gibberish, but still, pretty funny. 

Anyway, what was the question? Oh, arguing. Yeah, no, I don't really argue with cops or bosses or anything. I just do my job and try to get out of there.
